diff.title: Bulk storage put-away
diff.before:
1. Execute every bulk movement under PR-02 Put-away to storage without deviation from the system-directed location.
2. Complete system booking before any physical put-away to storage. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.
3. Direct all bulk-storage pallets to Zone B. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
4. Utilise only the location assigned by the warehouse system for each pallet. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions.
5. Confirm pallet weight against the system receipt before lifting to height. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg.
6. Observe the bay limit on every level during placement. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg.
7. Distribute heavy pallets to lower beam levels and never concentrate full-weight units in a single bay beyond its rating. Report any overload indication, deflection or impact damage immediately and quarantine the bay until cleared.
8. Apply free block-stack limits only where racking locations are not available and the system explicitly directs block stacking. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
9. Count units in the stack as well as height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
10. Align block stacks squarely, with base pallets fully supported and labels facing the aisle for scanning. Do not lean pallets against racking uprights or intrude into adjacent aisles.
11. Return damaged pallets, collapsed loads or overweight units to the inspection area for reassessment instead of forcing them into storage.
12. Log every put-away confirmation by scanner at the storage location. Investigate any mismatch between physical location and system location before leaving the aisle.
13. Protect racking integrity throughout all handling. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
14. Notify the maintenance technician at once of any upright damage, beam deformation, missing safety pins or anchor failure observed during PR-02 Put-away to storage. Record the bay identifier, retain photographs where safe to do so, and prevent further put-away to that bay until release.
15. Support the preventive regime for storage infrastructure. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.

diff.title: Hazmat cage and quarantine
diff.before:
1. Locate both controlled areas in Zone F. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and the quarantine area is in Zone F.
2. Recognise the shared setting. Zone F holds the value-added services area, so separate hazmat and quarantine stock physically from all rework, labelling and kitting activity.
3. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to every receipt, movement, check and spill in the cage. Do not substitute local practice for that procedure.
4. Respect the size of the enclosure. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2. Keep its boundary clear, locked and marked at all times.
5. Enforce the weight ceiling without exception. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6. Convert the ceiling into pallet planning before booking any pallet in. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg.
7. Calculate cage loading on full-weight units. The hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight).
8. Record inbound weight on the system receipt and verify the running cage total before transporting any additional pallet to the cage. Reject any movement that would breach the limit.
9. Segregate incompatible classes inside the cage using the designated bays and bunds. Stack only stable, sealed and labelled units on intact pallets.
10. Inspect the cage each shift for leaks, damaged packaging, missing labels and blocked access. Report defects immediately and contain spills exactly as PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response directs.
11. Use the quarantine area only for stock placed on system hold pending inspection, assessment or decision. Keep quarantined pallets clearly labelled and system-blocked against picking, replenishment and dispatch.
12. Prohibit direct put-away, picking or dispatch from quarantine. Move pallets out only after the authorised assessment releases them to their system-directed destination.
13. Count and secure both areas during stocktaking. Keep cage and quarantine locations closed to put-away and picking until their counts are closed.
14. Maintain separation between the two areas. Never store hazmat overflow in quarantine and never store quarantined general stock inside the hazmat cage to compensate for lack of racking space.

diff.title: Load and capacity limits
diff.before:
1. Apply this section to every load planned and released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
2. Limit each pallet, including its load, to at most 1000 kg.
3. Weigh or verify any suspect pallet before staging and remove overweight units from the outbound lane.
4. Plan contracted curtain-side trailers on a payload of 24000 kg.
5. Use 33 floor pallet positions as the physical floor limit for a trailer.
6. Load at most 24 full-weight pallets per trailer, determined by payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
7. Check both weight and floor positions on every trailer plan and apply the lower resulting limit.
8. Plan mixed lighter pallets against the same payload and floor limits and never exceed either constraint.
9. Plan the delivery van on a payload of 1200 kg.
10. Use 6 pallet positions as the physical floor limit for the delivery van.
11. Load at most 1 full-weight pallets in the van.
12. Transfer any heavier van order to trailer despatch and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.
13. Schedule each outbound door for 3 trailer loads per shift.
14. Operate with 4 outbound dock doors for outbound planning.
15. Cap outbound capacity at 288 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer.
16. Sequence door bookings to spread heavy pallets across loads and doors.
17. Reject any loading plan that exceeds trailer payload, van payload, floor positions, full-weight pallet maxima or the per-shift capacity.
18. Recalculate the plan when pallet weights change after wrapping, labelling or late additions.
19. Instruct loaders to stop loading when the verified weight or count reaches the applicable limit.
20. Record the final pallet count and gross weight for each released load in the system.

Under PR-06 Outbound dispatch weight governs before floor space where pallets are at maximum weight. A trailer offering 33 floor positions therefore departs full by weight at 24 full-weight pallets. Apply the same logic to the van, where payload restricts the van to 1 full-weight pallets despite 6 pallet positions.

Across 4 outbound dock doors at 3 trailer loads per shift, the site limit of 288 full-weight pallets per shift protects dock throughput, labour planning and vehicle availability. Build the daily despatch schedule backward from that ceiling. Prioritise timed collections within the ceiling and roll excess quantity to the next available load.

Validate every exception against pallet weight and trailer or van capacity before authorising an additional vehicle. Retain load calculations with the outbound documentation for traceability.

diff.title: Hazmat handling
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to every receipt, storage, movement and spill involving hazardous materials without exception.
2. Store all hazmat only inside the hazmat cage inside Zone F.
3. Treat the hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2 as a segregated controlled store and keep its boundaries, signage and access clear at all times.
4. Enforce the cage stock ceiling strictly during put-away, replenishment and returns transfer.
5. Verify that no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time before authorising any additional pallet movement inward.
6. Calculate the running cage total from system stock plus staged inbound pallets before transporting any further pallet to the cage.
7. Retain a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg as the planning figure for every hazmat pallet weight assessment.
8. Plan cage occupancy on the basis that the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight).
9. Reject any inbound or transferred pallet that would lift the cage above 4,000 kg and hold the excess pallet in the system-directed holding location pending release or onward instruction.
10. Check packaging integrity, labelling, compatibility and stability of each pallet before placement inside the 60 m2 cage.
11. Position compatible products together inside the cage and separate incompatible classes in accordance with the product safety data sheet.
12. Secure each pallet against movement, maintain clear access for inspection and emergency intervention, and never block cage doors or spill equipment.
13. Inspect the cage for leaks, damaged packaging, missing labels and blocked access before adding stock and after completing any handling task.
14. Initiate spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response immediately on discovering any leak, drip, damaged container or vapour release.
15. Stop all handling work in the affected area, warn personnel nearby, and prevent unauthorised entry to the spill zone.
16. Contain the spread using the designated spill materials where safe to do so and avoid allowing liquid to enter drains, aisles or adjacent storage.
17. Ventilate the area where instructed by the product safety data sheet and remove ignition sources where flammability is indicated.
18. Decontaminate affected packaging, equipment and floor surfaces only with approved materials and dispose of contaminated absorbents through the approved waste route.
19. Record the product identity, quantity involved, cage weight position, cause, containment actions and final disposition in the system promptly after the event.
20. Reconcile the cage running total after any loss, disposal or transfer out and confirm that no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat remains stored before resuming normal receipts.

diff.title: Operator Authorisation and Daily Checks
diff.before:
1. Operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks only when authorised as a forklift operator under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
2. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
3. Accountability of the warehouse manager covers the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including MHE authorisations.

4. Know your fleet before starting work:
(a) 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t;
(b) 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t;
(c) 8 electric pallet jacks;
(d) 12 hand pallet jacks.
Select the truck type rated for the load. Never exceed a pallet gross weight of 1000 kg, including its load.

5. Complete the documented pre-use check every day before first use of each forklift.
6. Carry out the same documented pre-use check each day before first use of each reach truck and each electric pallet jack.
7. Record each daily check in the designated log before moving the truck.
8. Isolate any truck with overdue planned maintenance, failed brakes, defective steering, damaged forks, faulty lights, leaking hydraulics or unreadable capacity plate.
9. Park defective MHE in the designated quarantine line and attach a do-not-use tag.
10. Notify the maintenance technician immediately about every defect found during checks or operation.
11. Understand that the maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
12. Wait for release by the maintenance technician before returning a quarantined truck to use.
13. Fasten your seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
14. Adjust mirrors, seat and steering position while stationary with the parking brake applied.
15. Test controls at low speed in a clear area after completing the daily check.
16. Report missing or illegible daily check sheets before starting operation.
17. Surrender authorisation documents on request during supervision checks.
18. Attend refresher briefing when instructed following any incident or observed unsafe act.
19. Comply with all further driving, speed and pedestrian rules in PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation before continuing duties on the floor.

diff.title: Racking and Stacking Limits
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-02 Put-away to storage for every pallet placed into bulk storage or block stack.
2. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
3. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions across the Zone B bays.
4. Verify the system-directed location before lifting any pallet to height.
5. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg.
6. Reject overweight units at the put-away face and return them for reassessment.
7. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg in total across all beam levels.
8. Distribute heavy pallets to lower beam levels within that bay limit.
9. Never concentrate full-weight pallets on upper beams where the bay total would be exceeded.
10. Use reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for placement and retrieval in the high bays.
11. Use counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t only where the aisle and rack configuration permits safe access.
12. Stop put-away immediately if the scanner shows the bay already at its rated load.
13. Apply free block stacking only where racking locations are not available and the system explicitly directs it.
14. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
15. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
16. Apply both block-stack limits together; exceeding either limit prohibits further stacking.
17. Align stacked pallets squarely face to face with no overhang or lean.
18. Keep block stacks clear of main transport aisles, rack storage aisles, pedestrian walkways, dock approaches and emergency exits.
19. Never climb racking or stacked pallets to reposition stock or labels.
20. Report any observed upright damage, beam deformation, missing safety pins or anchor failure to the maintenance technician at once.
21. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
22. Do not reload a damaged or overloaded bay until the maintenance technician has cleared and released it.
23. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.
24. Cooperate with the monthly inspection by clearing access and reporting defects found during PR-02 Put-away to storage.
25. Record beam impacts, scrapes or loose pallets found between inspections without delay.
26. In Zone B maintain safe separation between trucks and pedestrians during all put-away and retrieval movements.

diff.title: Hazmat Storage Limits
diff.before:
1. Store all hazardous materials only in the hazmat cage inside Zone F.
2. Do not store hazmat in any other zone, racking, staging lane, or general floor area.
3. Zone F holds the value-added services area, and the hazmat cage is the sole authorised location for hazmat within it.
4. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to every receipt, movement, inspection, and storage of hazmat.
5. Keep the hazmat cage inside Zone F clear, locked, signed, and accessible for inspection at all times.
6. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2; do not extend storage beyond its marked walls, doors, and floor markings.
7. Hold no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time.
8. Verify the running cage weight total before transporting any additional pallet to the hazmat cage.
9. Refuse any delivery to the cage that would take the total above 4,000 kg and segregate the excess outside the cage.
10. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg; use this limit when calculating cage capacity.
11. The hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets; treat four pallets at maximum weight as a full cage.
12. Record every pallet weight on receipt and maintain a visible running total at the cage entrance.
13. Update the running total immediately after each placement and each removal.
14. Inspect labelling, packaging integrity, and segregation inside the cage on every handling.
15. Report leaks, damaged packaging, missing labels, and blocked access for immediate action under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
16. Keep incompatible materials separated in line with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and label instructions.
17. Prohibit ignition sources, open flames, and unauthorised electrical equipment inside and immediately around the cage.
18. Allow entry only to trained personnel assigned to the hazmat task; exclude all other staff and visitors.
19. Wear the prescribed protective equipment for the material handled and ensure spill equipment is available before moving hazmat.
20. Transport hazmat pallets one at a time by the authorised route and place them directly into the designated cage position.
21. Do not stage hazmat pallets in aisles, dock areas, or Zone F work areas while awaiting cage space.
22. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including approval of any change to hazmat storage arrangements.
23. Obtain prior approval through the warehouse manager before accepting any new hazmat line or increased stock above planned levels.
24. Stop all further placements to the cage when the 4,000 kg limit or the 4 full-weight pallet limit is reached and escalate the overflow.
25. Never use general quarantine, bulk racking, or dispatch staging as overflow for hazmat.
26. Audit cage stock weight, pallet count, and documentation daily and correct any discrepancy before the next receipt.

We have reduced the maximum gross weight per pallet, including its load, from 1,000 kg to 800 kg.

notices.subject: New 800 kg maximum pallet weight - action for all site staff
notices.body:
Effective immediately, the maximum gross weight for any pallet including its load is reduced from 1000 kg to 800 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg.

All staff working on site are affected. Inbound operators must reject any pallet over 800 kg. Forklift operators, pickers and packing staff must check weight before lifting, stacking, wrapping or staging, and return overweight units for reassessment.

In practice this changes loading:

Warehouse Management, Harborwick 3PL Ltd.

Warehouse Manager, Harborwick 3PL Ltd.

diff.title: Load and capacity limits
diff.before:
1. Apply this section to every load planned and released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
2. Limit each pallet, including its load, to at most 800 kg.
3. Weigh or verify any suspect pallet before staging and remove overweight units from the outbound lane.
4. Plan contracted curtain-side trailers on a payload of 24000 kg.
5. Use 33 floor pallet positions as the physical floor limit for a trailer.
6. Load at most 30 full-weight pallets per trailer, determined by payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
7. Check both weight and floor positions on every trailer plan and apply the lower resulting limit.
8. Plan mixed lighter pallets against the same payload and floor limits and never exceed either constraint.
9. Plan the delivery van on a payload of 1200 kg.
10. Use 6 pallet positions as the physical floor limit for the delivery van.
11. Load at most 1 full-weight pallets in the van.

13. Schedule each outbound door for 3 trailer loads per shift.

15. Cap outbound capacity at 360 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer.
16. Sequence door bookings to spread heavy pallets across loads and doors.
17. Reject any loading plan that exceeds trailer payload, van payload, floor positions, full-weight pallet maxima or the per-shift capacity.
18. Recalculate the plan when pallet weights change after wrapping, labelling or late additions.
19. Instruct loaders to stop loading when the verified weight or count reaches the applicable limit.
20. Record the final pallet count and gross weight for each released load in the system.

diff.title: Management and supervision
diff.before:

2. During their assigned hours, the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Direction of inbound, storage, picking and dispatch tasks on the floor sits with the supervisor on duty. Escalation from operators goes to that supervisor in the first instance.

diff.title: Adjustments and racking
diff.before:
1. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments across all storage locations.
2. Complete a second count before any stock adjustment is posted under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
3. Never post an adjustment on a first count alone, even when the variance appears obvious from system stock or pick-face availability.
4. Record the approved recount result as the basis for the adjustment, retaining both count quantities in the system history for audit.
5. Route every adjustment arising from damage through PR-09 Damaged-goods handling before posting it against inventory.
6. Segregate the affected stock physically and systematically while the PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment is completed.
7. Obtain approval for the damaged-goods write-off before posting the corresponding stock adjustment.
8. Submit write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval and posting authority.
9. Escalate write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval, since that threshold requires higher authority.
10. Do not split a single damage event into smaller values to remain below the approval threshold.
11. Verify racking condition during every count round, noting upright impacts, beam deflection, missing pins and load distribution.
12. Respect the limit of 2,700 kg for each rack bay when confirming quantities during recounts and adjustments.

Adjustments must correct the system to verified physical reality, not to expected levels. Where recounts confirm overstock against pallets stored above bay limits, redistribute the load before posting the adjustment.

13. Report any damaged or overloaded bay found during counting to the maintenance technician at once and block that bay from further use.
14. Ensure the maintenance technician maintains racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs arising from count findings.
15. Support the documented racking safety inspection every month by making locations accessible and highlighting suspect bays.
16. Do not use the monthly inspection as a substitute for immediate reporting between inspections; escalate defects on discovery.
17. Hold unresolved adjustment items open to the next count cycle where recount evidence remains inconclusive, rather than forcing the balance.
18. Confirm that approved adjustments are reflected in the system before releasing affected locations back to put-away or picking.

diff.title: Damaged goods
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling to every crushed carton, leaking unit, collapsed pallet, water-affected pack and suspected contamination found on receipt, in storage, at picking or on return.
2. Move the affected stock to the quarantine area in Zone F on the same shift it is found, keeping pallet integrity and labels intact for assessment.
3. Record the date, location found, product code, quantity, damage type, photographs where required, and the discovering operator in the system quarantine record.
4. Segregate damaged units from saleable stock inside quarantine, preventing any put-away, replenishment, picking or dispatch until assessment is complete.
5. Assign assessment without delay to trained personnel on the shift, preserving cold-chain or hazmat controls during the transfer where applicable.
6. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap, completing that inspection BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision is taken.
7. Assess all other damaged goods on the same basis: confirm quantity and condition first, then recommend restock to saleable locations, rework in the designated area, or scrap with stated reason.
8. Obtain written write-off approval before scrapping or adjusting any value from inventory, attaching the assessment and supporting evidence to the request.
9. Send write-offs valued up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval, providing the quarantine reference, quantities and calculated value.
10. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval, since damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval and must not proceed on lower authority.
11. Confirm that the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR and the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR, routing each case strictly by its total value.
12. Post the approved disposition on the same day wherever the shift allows: release restock to its system-directed location, transfer rework to its holding position, and remove scrapped units through the authorised scrap route.
13. Retain the quarantine record, assessment, approval and system adjustment together for audit, linking the stock adjustment to the PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment that authorised it.
14. Review open quarantine positions at each shift handover, carrying unresolved assessments forward with named owner and required completion time until closure.

diff.title: Spills, Quarantine and Damaged Goods
diff.before:
1. Stop work in the affected area immediately when you discover a leak, spill or damaged container. Warn nearby personnel, eliminate ignition sources where safe to do so, and prevent the substance spreading to aisles, drains or other zones.

2. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every chemical, fuel, battery-acid or unidentified liquid spill. Follow the spill-kit instructions for containment and absorption, wear the specified protective equipment, and ventilate the area as directed.

3. Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Do not attempt clean-up beyond your training; wait for instruction and handover control of the scene on arrival.

4. Segregate all suspect, leaking, temperature-affected or damaged stock at once. Move affected pallets and cartons to quarantine, using clean handling equipment to avoid cross-contamination.

5. Place all quarantined stock only in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not leave quarantined goods in receiving, bulk storage, picking or dispatch aisles, on dock approaches or in pedestrian walkways.

6. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep quarantine, inspection, rework and value-added tasks physically separated within Zone F. Maintain clear access to the quarantine area for inspection and removal at all times.

7. Returns are inspected in Zone F. Transfer inbound returns directly to the inspection point and hold them there until disposition is decided. Do not restock, rework or scrap any return before inspection is complete.

8. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the inspection result, quantity, condition and proposed disposition in the system and attach the disposition label to each unit.

9. Execute PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for every damaged, crushed, punctured, wet or contaminated unit found on receipt, in storage, during picking or on return. Photograph the damage, retain packaging and labels where safe, and enter the full quantity and value in the damage record.

10. Obtain write-off approval before scrapping or adjusting any damaged stock. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

11. Apply the approval threshold to each damage event separately. Do not divide one event to remain within a lower limit. Escalate any dispute over value or responsibility to the shift supervisor for decision.

12. Release quarantined stock only on written authorisation in the system. Return cleared goods to their directed location, send approved rework to the designated position, and dispatch scrap through the controlled route. Review every spill and damage event at shift handover and close all open quarantine records before the next shift starts.

notices.subject: Staff memo: Damaged-goods write-off threshold now 750 EUR
notices.body:
Colleagues - the damaged-goods write-off threshold has changed.

From now on the limit is 750 EUR per damage event, increased from 500 EUR. Do not use the old 500 EUR limit.

What this means in practice:
- For any write-off valued up to 750 EUR, get approval from the shift supervisor on duty before scrapping or adjusting stock. Record the decision in the damage log.
- For any write-off valued above 750 EUR, escalate to the warehouse manager for approval. Do not scrap, discount or adjust stock before that approval is granted.
- Apply the limit to each damage event separately. Do not split one event into smaller values to stay below the threshold.

diff.title: Load and capacity limits
diff.before:
1. Apply this section to every load planned and released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
2. Limit each pallet, including its load, to at most 800 kg.
3. Weigh or verify any suspect pallet before staging and remove overweight units from the outbound lane.
4. Plan contracted curtain-side trailers on a payload of 22000 kg.
5. Use 33 floor pallet positions as the physical floor limit for a trailer.
6. Load at most 27 full-weight pallets per trailer, determined by payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
7. Check both weight and floor positions on every trailer plan and apply the lower resulting limit.
8. Plan mixed lighter pallets against the same payload and floor limits and never exceed either constraint.
9. Plan the delivery van on a payload of 1200 kg.
10. Use 6 pallet positions as the physical floor limit for the delivery van.
11. Load at most 1 full-weight pallets in the van.
12. Transfer any heavier van order to trailer despatch and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.
13. Schedule each outbound door for 3 trailer loads per shift.
14. Operate with 4 outbound dock doors for outbound planning.
15. Cap outbound capacity at 324 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer.
16. Sequence door bookings to spread heavy pallets across loads and doors.
17. Reject any loading plan that exceeds trailer payload, van payload, floor positions, full-weight pallet maxima or the per-shift capacity.
18. Recalculate the plan when pallet weights change after wrapping, labelling or late additions.
19. Instruct loaders to stop loading when the verified weight or count reaches the applicable limit.
20. Record the final pallet count and gross weight for each released load in the system.

Under PR-06 Outbound dispatch weight governs before floor space where pallets are at maximum weight. A trailer offering 33 floor positions therefore departs full by weight at 27 full-weight pallets. Apply the same logic to the van, where payload restricts the van to 1 full-weight pallets despite 6 pallet positions.

Across 4 outbound dock doors at 3 trailer loads per shift, the site limit of 324 full-weight pallets per shift protects dock throughput, labour planning and vehicle availability. Build the daily despatch schedule backward from that ceiling. Prioritise timed collections within the ceiling and roll excess quantity to the next available load.

diff.title: Outbound Dispatch Capacity and Cut-Offs
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. undertakes outbound dispatch from Zone D, which provides outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

2. Across the building Harborwick operates 8 dock doors, with dock doors 5-8 dedicated to outbound dispatch.

3. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for loading under this agreement.

4. Dispatch operates across two shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

5. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads for both shifts.

6. For every outbound movement the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, and carriers are loaded only against that assigned door and slot.

7. All orders are prepared under PR-05 Packing and labelling before handover to PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging and loading.

8. To protect load integrity dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers for outbound pallets.

9. For safe vehicle interfacing each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller, including all outbound doors.

10. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound loads carry a payload of 22000 kg and provide 33 floor pallet positions.

11. Because a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg, a trailer takes at most 27 full-weight pallets.

12. Our delivery van used for small consignments carries a payload of 1200 kg and has 6 pallet positions.

13. On that basis the van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

14. Within these equipment limits each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.

15. Accordingly outbound capacity is at most 324 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated from doors, loads per shift and pallets per trailer.

16. Lighter pallets may use more of the available floor positions up to the stated trailer and van limits, subject to weight, stability and dispatcher confirmation.

17. A staging lane is released for loading only after the dispatcher has released that outbound load in the system.

18. Loads not released by the dispatcher-confirmed cut-off time for the booked slot will be rebooked to the next available door and slot, with the client notified of the revised departure.

notices.subject: Increased outbound dispatch capacity per shift
notices.body:
Dear clients,

We have increased outbound dispatch capacity with immediate effect.

Each outbound door now handles 4 trailer loads per shift, previously 3 loads. Accordingly, outbound capacity is now at most 432 full-weight pallets per shift, previously 324 pallets. This is calculated from 4 outbound dock doors x 4 loads per shift x 27 full-weight pallets per trailer.

In practice, more of your orders can be staged, released and loaded within the same shift, reducing the need to roll quantity to the next available load. Lighter pallets may continue to use more floor positions subject to weight, stability and dispatcher confirmation.

Loads not released by the dispatcher-confirmed cut-off for the booked slot will continue to be rebooked to the next available door and slot, with notification of the revised departure.

The new limits are set out in the Client Service Level Agreement, section Outbound Dispatch Capacity and Cut-Offs.

Thank you for your business.

Warehouse Management, Harborwick 3PL Ltd.

notices.subject: Outbound doors now 4 loads per shift - 432 pallets per shift limit
notices.body:
All site staff – dispatch, loading and shift teams – must work to the new outbound rate.

Each outbound door now handles 4 trailer loads per shift, up from 3 loads. With 4 outbound dock doors and a limit of 27 full-weight pallets per trailer, outbound capacity is now at most 432 full-weight pallets per shift, up from 324 pallets, calculated as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer.

In practice build the daily despatch schedule backward from the 432-pallet ceiling, spread heavy pallets across loads and doors, prioritise timed collections within the ceiling and roll excess quantity to the next available load. Reject any loading plan that exceeds trailer payload, floor positions or the per-shift capacity, and stop loading when verified weight or count reaches the limit. Record the final pallet count and gross weight for each released load.

This rule is now set in Operations Manual - Load and capacity limits, Job Descriptions - Warehouse Manager and Job Descriptions - Dispatcher, and Client Service Level Agreement - Outbound Dispatch Capacity and Cut-Offs.

Warehouse Manager, Harborwick 3PL Ltd.
